topic_title: Garland Christmas Ideas: 10 Ways to Hang It Around the House
intro: Garland does more than most decorations for its price because one length can frame a whole doorway, mantel or banister. The two things that decide how it looks are fullness and fixing. Thin garland looks sparse once it is draped, so plan on layering two strands or tucking in picks. Fixing matters because garland is heavier than it looks, especially pre-lit versions, so measure the run, add a foot or two for draping, and choose hooks rated for the weight before you hang anything.

picks.breed: Faux Cedar Garland on the Mantel
picks.description: The mantel is where garland has the most impact, because it frames the fireplace that already pulls attention in the room. A six- or nine-foot faux cedar garland drapes more softly than stiff pine, and its flat sprays lie well along a shelf. Lay it along the mantel, let the ends fall down each side by a foot or more, and hold it with mantel clips or weighted hooks rather than nails. For fullness, layer a second strand of a different green, such as eucalyptus, and weave warm white lights through both. Keep everything a safe distance above the firebox if you use the fireplace, since faux greenery can still melt or scorch. The trade-off is that a bare strand looks thin from across a room, so plan on layering or adding a few picks.
picks.best_for: Living rooms with a fireplace or a shelf above a TV console
picks.skip_if: You light the fireplace often and the mantel sits low over the flames
picks.quirky_fact: Draping garland so the ends hang to different lengths on each side looks more natural than a perfectly even swag.
picks.product_name: National Tree Company Faux Cedar Garland, 9 Feet

picks.breed: Pre-Lit Garland Around the Front Door
picks.description: A pre-lit garland around the front door greets guests and shows from the street after dark. Most door surrounds take about 15 to 18 feet: two sides plus the top. Battery-operated versions with a timer avoid running an extension cord across the porch, while plug-in sets suit doors with a nearby outdoor outlet. Hold the top run with an over-the-door hook or gutter-style clips on the trim, and use outdoor-rated adhesive hooks down the sides. Choose a garland labelled for outdoor use, since indoor versions can fade and their wiring is not built for rain. The trade-off is weight and wind: heavy pre-lit garland pulls at cheap hooks, so check ratings and add an extra hook at each corner. Pair it with a wreath of the same green for a matched look.
picks.best_for: Covered porches and doorways that face the street
picks.skip_if: Your door is fully exposed to heavy wind and you rent with strict exterior rules
picks.quirky_fact: Many battery garlands have a six-hours-on, eighteen-off timer, so they switch on at the same time every evening.
picks.product_name: National Tree Company Pre-Lit Crestwood Spruce Garland, Battery Operated, 9 Feet

picks.breed: Garland Wrapped on the Staircase Banister
picks.description: A staircase banister gives garland a long, sloping line that looks generous without any extra props. Measure the handrail and add about half again for gentle swags, or nearly double for a full spiral wrap. Tie the garland on every 12 to 18 inches with green floral wire, clear zip ties or velvet ribbon bows, which hold it without marking the wood. Keep the top of the handrail clear enough to grip, because people still need to use the stairs safely, so drape on the outer side of the balusters rather than over the rail itself. Lights work well here but need a nearby outlet at the top or bottom. The trade-off is that banister garland collects bumps from passing traffic and pets, so choose a durable faux strand rather than fresh greens that shed needles on the steps.
picks.best_for: Homes with an open staircase visible from the entry or living room
picks.skip_if: Small children or older relatives rely on a fully clear handrail
picks.quirky_fact: Tying the garland to the outside of the balusters keeps the handrail usable while still showing from the hallway.
picks.product_name: National Tree Company Norwood Fir Garland, 9 Feet

picks.breed: Eucalyptus Garland as a Table Runner
picks.description: A faux eucalyptus garland laid straight down the center of the dining table works as a runner that is softer and quieter than tartan or tinsel. Silver-green eucalyptus suits both Christmas and the rest of winter, so it can stay out from Thanksgiving through January. Run it the length of the table, then set pillar candles in glass hurricanes, small ornaments or pine cones along it. Keep open flames inside glass, since faux leaves catch fire easily. A five- or six-foot garland covers most six-seat tables; two can be overlapped for longer ones. The trade-off is that a low runner can get crowded once dishes arrive, so keep decorations narrow and leave room for serving platters or move items to a sideboard before dinner.
picks.best_for: Dining tables that host Thanksgiving and Christmas meals
picks.skip_if: Your table is small and every inch is needed for dishes
picks.quirky_fact: Eucalyptus garland reads as winter rather than strictly Christmas, so it can stay out well into January.
picks.product_name: Ivenf Faux Eucalyptus Garland, 6 Feet, Pack of 2

picks.description: A dried orange slice garland glows when light passes through it, which makes it best in a sunny window, across open shelves or on the tree. You can buy one ready-made or make your own by slicing oranges thinly, drying them in a low oven for several hours until firm, then threading them with twine, often alternating with cinnamon sticks, bay leaves or wood beads. Homemade slices need to be fully dry or they can mold in a humid room. The color fades from bright orange to amber over a season, which many people like. The trade-off is fragility: dried slices crack if crushed in storage, so wrap the garland around a piece of cardboard and keep it in a dry box. Hang it high in homes with pets, since dogs may chew it.
picks.best_for: Cottage, rustic and Scandinavian-style rooms with good daylight
picks.skip_if: You have a pet that chews things within reach or a damp storage space
picks.quirky_fact: Slicing oranges about a quarter inch thick is thin enough to dry evenly yet thick enough not to curl.
picks.product_name: Dried Orange Slice Garland with Cinnamon Sticks, 6 Feet

picks.breed: Wood Bead Garland on the Tree
picks.description: Wood bead garland drapes across a tree in loose swags and adds texture that lights and ornaments do not. Natural wood looks calm with white lights and simple ornaments; painted or mixed-tone beads suit a more playful tree. Start at the top and let each loop dip about a hand's width before catching it on a branch, working down and around. Most strands are five to six feet, so a seven-foot tree usually takes three to five. Bead garland is also useful away from the tree, coiled in a dough bowl, hung on a cabinet knob or draped over a picture frame. It is light, nearly unbreakable and packs into a small bag, so it lasts for years. The trade-off is that it adds little sparkle on its own, so it works best alongside lights.
picks.best_for: Neutral, farmhouse or Scandinavian Christmas trees
picks.skip_if: You want a glamorous metallic tree with lots of shine
picks.quirky_fact: Wood bead garland survives being stepped on, which makes it a favorite for homes with toddlers.
picks.product_name: Wood Bead Garland with Tassels, Natural Farmhouse, 6 Feet

picks.breed: Pine Cone Garland on a Shelf
picks.description: Pine cone garland adds a woodland texture to bookshelves, window ledges and the top of a hutch, where loose cones would roll away. Ready-made versions string natural or frosted cones on twine or wire, often mixed with berries or faux pine. Drape it along the front edge of a shelf so the cones hang slightly over, or loop it around a lantern or framed print. It also layers well over a plain green garland on the mantel. Natural cones can carry dust or small insects if you gather your own, so bake foraged cones in a low oven before stringing them. The trade-off is weight distribution: cones are heavier than greenery, so check that hooks or shelf edges can hold the strand without sagging. Store it in a box rather than a bag so cones are not crushed.
picks.best_for: Bookshelves, hutches and window ledges that need a rustic touch
picks.skip_if: You prefer a sleek modern look with no natural textures
picks.quirky_fact: Pine cones close up in damp air and open in dry air, so a heated room tends to keep them open.
picks.product_name: Pine Cone Garland with Red Berries, 6 Feet

picks.breed: Felt Ball Garland in a Kids' Room
picks.description: Felt ball garland is soft, colorful and light enough to hang with a single small removable hook at each end, which makes it a good fit for kids' rooms and nurseries. Strands are usually made of wool or wool-blend balls about an inch wide on cotton thread, in red and white for Christmas or in rainbow mixes that stay up year-round. Swag it above a bed, across a bookcase or around a small tree in the child's room. Because it is soft and has no wires or glass, it is safer near children than most garlands, though the small balls should stay out of reach of babies and toddlers who put things in their mouths. The trade-off is scale: felt ball garland looks small from across a large room, so keep it for close-up spots.
picks.best_for: Kids' bedrooms, playrooms and small reading nooks
picks.skip_if: You have a baby or toddler who could pull it down and chew the balls
picks.quirky_fact: Felt balls are made by rolling loose wool in warm soapy water until the fibers lock together.
picks.product_name: Christmas Felt Ball Garland, Red and White, 2 cm Balls

picks.description: A short garland across the top of the kitchen window brings Christmas to the room where people spend much of the holiday without taking up counter space. Four to six feet usually covers a standard window, with the ends tucked behind the frame or allowed to hang a little at each side. Hold it with removable hooks on the trim or a tension rod set inside the frame. Choose faux greenery here, since kitchen heat and steam dry out fresh garland fast, and keep it well away from the stove. A battery light strand woven through avoids an extra cord near the sink. The trade-off is grease and dust: kitchen garland gets grimy, so give it a shake outdoors and wipe the hooks before packing it away.
picks.best_for: Kitchens with a window over the sink or breakfast nook
picks.skip_if: The window sits right beside the stove or a gas burner
picks.quirky_fact: A tension rod inside the window frame holds a light garland with no hooks or adhesive at all.
picks.product_name: Battery Operated Pre-Lit Mini Pine Garland, 6 Feet, Warm White

picks.description: Stringing popcorn and fresh cranberries is the classic handmade garland, cheap to make and a good evening activity with children. Use plain air-popped popcorn that has cooled and dried for a day so it threads without crumbling, a large needle and strong thread or fishing line, and alternate a few kernels with each cranberry. A cup of cranberries and a big bowl of popcorn make a strand several feet long. It looks best looped on a tree with simple ornaments. The trade-off is that it does not last: popcorn goes stale and cranberries soften within a couple of weeks indoors, so it is a one-season decoration that goes in the compost after Christmas. Keep it out of reach of pets and away from pets' feeding areas.
picks.best_for: Families wanting a cheap, hands-on project for a December evening
picks.skip_if: You want a garland that can be packed away and reused next year
picks.quirky_fact: Popcorn that has sat out for a day threads more easily because fresh popcorn crumbles around the needle.
picks.product_name: Ocean Spray Fresh Cranberries, 12 oz Bag

faqs.question: How long should Christmas garland be for a mantel?
faqs.answer: Measure the mantel shelf and add about one to two feet on each side if you want the ends to drape down. A five-foot mantel usually takes a six- or nine-foot garland. If you want a full swag that dips in the middle, add more length again. Buying two shorter strands and overlapping them in the center is often easier to adjust than one long piece.

faqs.question: How do you hang garland without nails?
faqs.answer: Use removable adhesive hooks rated for the garland's weight, placed every 12 to 18 inches, or command-style mantel clips that grip the shelf edge. On banisters, green floral wire, zip ties or ribbon tie it on without touching the wood. For a front door, an over-the-door hook can hold the top while adhesive hooks hold the sides. Always check the weight rating before buying hooks.

faqs.question: How can I make cheap garland look fuller?
faqs.answer: Fluff every branch tip outward after unboxing, then layer a second garland or a strand of eucalyptus or cedar picks over the first. Weave a string of warm white lights through it, and tuck in pine cones, ornaments or ribbon at even spacing. Two inexpensive strands twisted together usually look fuller than one premium strand on its own.

faqs.question: Is fresh garland or faux garland better?
faqs.answer: Fresh garland smells good and looks natural, but it dries out within two to four weeks indoors and drops needles, especially near heat. Faux garland costs more up front but can be reused for years, and it is safer near lights and fireplaces. A common compromise is faux garland with a few fresh cedar or eucalyptus sprigs tucked in for scent.

faqs.question: Are edible garlands safe around pets?
faqs.answer: Popcorn, cranberry and dried orange garlands can attract dogs and cats, and the string or thread used in them can be a hazard if swallowed. Hang them high on the tree or out of reach, or choose wood bead and felt garlands in homes with curious pets.

seo_title: Garland Christmas Ideas 2026: 10 Ways to Hang It
answer: The most useful places for Christmas garland are the mantel, the front door and the staircase banister, because each one frames something people already look at. The deciding factor is how you will attach it: pick spots where removable hooks, ties or the furniture itself can hold the weight without nails.
